title: Here’s how an Ethereum upgrade helped drain part of Binance’s $6 billion loss
summary: Title: Here’s how an Ethereum upgrade helped drain part of Binance’s $6 billion loss URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/10/30/here-s-how-one-ethereum-permission-let-an-attacker-drain-usd2-5-billion-from-binance Published Time: 2026-10-30T11:35:16.645Z Markdown Content: Oct 30, 2026, 7:35 a.m. EDT 4 min read ![Image 1: Picture of a phone displaying the Binance app. (Shutterstock)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Fc21fed99fa765785749736d4a3023e5aed2b83af-1500x1000.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C78%2C1500%2C844%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=1200&q=75) Here’s how one Ethereum permission let an attacker drain $2.5 billion from Binance. (Shutterstock) Summary * An attacker used Ethereum’s EIP-7702 feature, which lets ordinary wallets run smart-contract code, to drain about $2.5 billion from a Binance wallet in less than four minutes on Thursday. * The attacker obtained valid signatures authorizing malicious code that remained active for nearly four hours, allowing further thefts as customer deposits continued arriving. * Binance put losses across several blockchains at $6.3 billion and pledged to cover them, while investigators continue examining how the attacker obtained authorization to move the funds. A Binance wallet signed a permission on Thursday that let an attacker-controlled contract operate it. Less than four minutes later, about $2.5 billion in ether and tokens was gone. That was only part of the roughly $6.3 billion Binance says was stolen across several blockchains. On Ethereum, the attacker used a feature called EIP-7702, named for its Ethereum Improvement Proposal number. It went live in May 2025 as part of the Pectra upgrade. To see why it mattered on Thursday, lets start with what an ordinary Ethereum wallet is. ## Wallet goes rogue Most Ethereum wallets, from a retail user's browser wallet to an exchange's hot wallet, are controlled by a private key.
